authors: Costello, T. H., Pennycook, G., & Rand, D. G.
title: Durably reducing conspiracy beliefs through dialogues with AI
summary: A single AI-driven conversation can durably reduce conspiracy beliefs with effects persisting two months later using a general-purpose LLM without a curated technique corpus.
relevance_reason: Closest empirical precedent for AI-driven belief change via dialogue; our work extends it by making strategy selection explicit rather than implicit in pretraining.

title: Multi-LLM Debate: Framework Principals and Interventions
summary: Multi-agent debate improves LLM reasoning but agents sharing a training distribution converge on shared biases rather than reaching better answers.
relevance_reason: Motivates our shared-bias limitation; also provides the multi-agent debate framing our system extends toward belief intervention.

authors: Gorwa, R., Binns, R., & Katzenbach, C.
title: Algorithmic content moderation: Technical and political challenges in the automation of platform governance
summary: Documents the technical and political limitations of automated content moderation as a governance tool for harmful online speech.
relevance_reason: Establishes that content-level moderation is insufficient — motivates belief-level intervention as a complementary approach.

title: Curiosity-driven Red-teaming for Large Language Models
summary: Automatically generated adversarial prompts can elicit unsafe outputs from well-performing LLMs motivating robust intervention mechanisms.
relevance_reason: Shows LLMs are vulnerable to adversarial inputs; motivates need for structured technique constraints rather than unconstrained generation.

title: Atlas: Few-shot Learning with Retrieval Augmented Language Models
summary: Retrieved passages substantially improve LLM generation on knowledge-intensive tasks establishing the grounding motivation for RAG.
relevance_reason: Foundational RAG citation motivating both retrieval channels in our system.

authors: Kumar, D., AbuHashem, Y., & Durumeric, Z.
title: Watch Your Language: Investigating Content Moderation with Large Language Models
summary: Instruction-tuned LLMs outperform traditional classifiers on toxicity detection but remain sensitive to context shifts.
relevance_reason: Situates our work relative to detection-oriented LLM moderation; we operate at the belief layer rather than the content layer.

title: Police Interrogation and American Justice
summary: Documents the Reid Technique's history and criticisms particularly regarding false confessions in real interrogation contexts.
relevance_reason: Primary source for the Reid Technique used in our corpus; also motivates our exclusion of coercive steps on ethical grounds.

authors: Oleszkiewicz, S., Granhag, P. A., & Kleinman, S. M.
title: On Eliciting Intelligence from Human Sources: Contextualizing the Scharff-Technique
summary: Formalizes the Scharff Technique showing that implying familiarity rather than direct questioning elicits more information from sources.
relevance_reason: Direct source for the Scharff-style indirect argument deployment used in our Stage-2 generator.

title: Like Sheep Among Wolves: Characterizing Hateful Users on Twitter
summary: A small number of high-centrality accounts in hateful Twitter communities are responsible for a disproportionate share of content propagation.
relevance_reason: Motivates selective high-centrality targeting as an economically viable deployment strategy; directly cited in our future work.

title: Explicit Time Embedding Based Cascade Attention Network for Information Popularity Prediction
summary: Combines timing information with network structure to estimate how widely content will spread in online networks.
relevance_reason: Dynamic graph learning tool for modeling influence propagation — part of the upstream targeting pipeline described in future work.

title: Towards Better Dynamic Graph Learning: New Architecture and Unified Library
summary: Provides architecture and unified library for dynamic graph learning to model how influence evolves through networks over time.
relevance_reason: Companion to Sun et al. for the network targeting upstream component described in future work.

title: Counter-Radicalization Bot Research: Using Social Bots to Fight Violent Extremism
summary: Studies using social bots to rapidly detect targets of violent extremist recruitment and deliver counter-radicalization content; analyzes feasibility legal and ethical considerations of bot-based CVE.
relevance_reason: Closest prior system to ours in the CVE space; bots lacked principled turn-by-turn strategy selection — our RAG recommender adds exactly that layer.

title: AI-Based Deradicalization: Opportunities Risks and Case Studies
primary_venue: Journal of Digital Security and Forensics 2(2)
summary: Reviews AI opportunities in deradicalization including conversational agents; identifies evaluation as a recurring gap across all case studies.
relevance_reason: Explicitly identifies conversational agents as an opportunity and evaluation as an unsolved problem — both directly addressed by our work.

authors: Kolenik, T., Schiepek, G., & Gams, M.
title: Computational Psychotherapy System for Mental Health Prediction and Behavior Change with a Conversational Agent
summary: Builds a conversational agent that selects therapeutic interventions based on a simulated theory of mind modeling user mental state.
relevance_reason: Structural precedent for turn-by-turn strategy selection inside a dialogue agent; ours differs in domain (ideological vs emotional) and mechanism (RAG vs cognitive architecture).

title: Unraveling SITT: Social Influence Technique Taxonomy and Detection with LLMs
summary: Builds a taxonomy of 58 social influence techniques and evaluates LLM ability to detect them in dialogue; finds LLMs are only moderately capable.
relevance_reason: Shows LLMs cannot reliably identify influence techniques implicitly — motivates our explicit RAG-based technique retrieval rather than relying on model knowledge.

authors: Nicholson, J., Keeling, S., & Black, M.
title: Countering Violent Extremism Online: Understanding Adversity and Adaptation in an Increasingly Complex Digital Environment
summary: Documents that coordinated deplatforming has driven extremists to less monitored alternative platforms hardening rather than dissolving extremist networks.
relevance_reason: Institutional evidence that content-removal approaches are counterproductive — directly motivates belief-level intervention as an alternative.

title: From TikTok to Terrorism? The Online Radicalization of European Lone Attackers since October 7 2023
summary: Documents algorithm-driven affective identity-forming radicalization on TikTok linked to lone-actor attacks in Europe 2023-2025; existing P/CVE strategies proved insufficient.
relevance_reason: Concrete recent evidence of the radicalization pattern motivating our work; shows identity-protective affective radicalization resistant to content-level responses.

title: Why Do Online Countering Violent Extremism Strategies Not Work? The Case of Digital Jihad
summary: Argues that the three pillars of online CVE (counter-narratives awareness-raising takedowns) have produced few tangible results particularly content control.
relevance_reason: Establishes that the third CVE pillar (takedowns) fails; motivates a fourth pillar of individualized dialogue intervention.

title: Psychological Underpinnings of Misinformation Countermeasures
summary: Reviews 176 misinformation interventions finding most are poorly linked to psychological theory and not designed to address motivated reasoning specifically.
relevance_reason: Motivates theory-grounded technique selection; gap between intervention practice and psychological theory is exactly what our corpus addresses.

title: Misinformation and Its Correction
summary: Documents the worldview backfire effect where corrections contradicting prior beliefs can strengthen rather than weaken them in identity-protective contexts.
relevance_reason: Provides the psychological mechanism explaining why direct argument fails on extremist beliefs and why indirect rapport-based techniques are necessary.

title: The Mathematics of Political Mayhem
summary: Presents a computational framework combining Bayesian inference Markov chains and network analysis to predict stochastic violence from extremist network structure.
relevance_reason: Provides mathematical grounding for high-centrality targeting; maps extremist networks to identify nodes whose rhetoric diffuses most widely.

title: AI Agents for Counter-Extremism: Deployment Frameworks for Covert and Overt Digital Deradicalisation
summary: Evaluates three AI agent deployment models (overt analytical direct engagement covert) across technical legal ethical and strategic dimensions; recommends transparent community-partnered approaches.
relevance_reason: Provides taxonomy locating our system as a direct engagement agent; argues this is the most strategically effective approach while being legally defensible.

title: PROTOCOL: Interventions Targeting Misinformation, Disinformation and Malinformation for Reducing and Countering Violent Extremism: A Systematic Review
summary: Protocol for a systematic review of MDM interventions and violent extremism; signals active research frontier at intersection of communication and CVE.
relevance_reason: Signals this is an active research frontier; our work contributes empirical evidence to the gap the review will synthesize.

authors: Scheele, R., Voogd, A., & Berends, A. (RAN Practitioners Staff)
title: AI: Understanding and Opportunities for P/CVE Practitioners
summary: EU practitioner network meeting report identifying AI opportunities for P/CVE work; calls for conversational chatbots and knowledge-base tools while noting AI is currently over-securitised and under-used for positive intervention.
relevance_reason: Institutional evidence from EU practitioners that conversational AI tools are needed but absent in P/CVE — directly motivates our system from a policy rather than academic angle.

authors: Chen, W., Wang, Y., & Zhou, T.
title: Beyond Reactive Empathy: Efficient RL for Proactive Emotion-Adaptive and LLM-based Mental Health Chatbot Design
summary: Builds a mental health chatbot that selects conversational strategies proactively using RL within a POMDP framework maintaining beliefs about latent emotional states and optimizing strategy selection over multiple turns; outperforms reactive LLM baselines.
relevance_reason: Closest structural precedent to our two-stage select-then-generate pipeline; distinguishes from ours in domain (emotional vs ideological) mechanism (RL vs RAG) and corpus (learned vs explicit auditable technique cards).

authors: Sinai, J., Fuller, J., & Seal, T.
title: Research Note: Effectiveness in Counter-Terrorism and Countering Violent Extremism: A Literature Review
summary: Literature review of 200+ CT/CVE publications identifying consistent gap between process metrics (reach disruption) and outcome metrics (attitude and behavior change); notes soft CVE approaches lack rigorous evaluation.
relevance_reason: Reinforces the evaluation gap cluster (with Koehler 2017 Helmus & Klein 2018 Bateman & Jackson 2024) that your controlled experimental design directly addresses.

authors: Chuang, Y. S., Tu, R., Dai, C., Li, Y., Vasani, S., Yao, B., Tessler, M. H., Yang, S., Shah, D., Hawkins, R., Hu, J., & Rogers, T. T.
title: DEBATE: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Evaluating Opinion Dynamics in Role-Playing LLM Agents
field: NLP / computational social science / opinion dynamics
summary: Introduces a large-scale benchmark of 2788 participants across 107 topics for evaluating authenticity of opinion dynamics in multi-agent RPLA simulations; finds that RPLAs exhibit premature convergence and unnatural stance alignment relative to humans.
relevance_reason: Directly motivates and formalizes our LLM-vs-LLM evaluation limitation; RPLA convergence artifacts it identifies are exactly the confound our directional accuracy metric partially guards against.

authors: Hackenburg, K., Tappin, B. M., Hewitt, L., Saunders, E., Black, S., Lin, H., Fist, C., Margetts, H., Rand, D. G., & Summerfield, C.
title: The Levers of Political Persuasion with Conversational AI
field: NLP / political psychology / computational social science
summary: Large-scale study (N=76,977) across 19 LLMs and 707 political issues showing conversational AI is 41-52% more persuasive than static messages with durable effects; post-training and prompting drive persuasiveness more than model scale or personalization.
relevance_reason: Empirically validates our core premise (conversational AI persuasion works and is durable); their finding that structured prompting boosts persuasiveness directly supports why RAG-guided technique selection should outperform an unguided baseline.

authors: Lindsay, G., Brown, J. C., Johnson, B. D., Owens, C., Hall, A., & Carrott, J. H.
title: Microtargeting Unmasked: Safeguarding Law Enforcement the Military and the Nation in the Era of Personalized Threats
primary_venue: ASU Threatcasting Lab / US Secret Service / Army Cyber Institute (Threatcasting Lab Report)
summary: Threatcasting report examining how adversaries use personalized microtargeting to attack high-value individuals; documents the dual-use nature of persuasion technology and identifies mitigation strategies.
relevance_reason: Frames the dual-use problem your system raises — targeted belief-level persuasion can serve either protective or manipulative ends; the Bernays appendix contextualizes the historical roots of engineered consent that your system transparently inverts.

title: Threatcasting: a framework and process to model future operating environments
primary_venue: Journal of Defense Modeling and Simulation: Applications Methodology Technology
summary: A foresight methodology combining backcasting scenario planning and Delphi methods to model future threats and specify actionable mitigation steps; developed at ASU and the Army Cyber Institute at West Point.
relevance_reason: Provides a foresight vocabulary for situating our dialogue intervention within a broader counter-extremism strategy pipeline; the TAD backcasting phase maps loosely to the upstream network targeting + downstream dialogue intervention sequence.

authors: European Commission Expert Group on Violent Radicalisation (Reinares, F. et al.)
title: Radicalisation Processes Leading to Acts of Terrorism
primary_venue: European Commission Expert Group Report (submitted 15 May 2008)
summary: Foundational EU policy report reviewing academic research on violent radicalisation; concludes it is driven by rational emotional and identitarian motivations in combination and calls for persuasive non-radical narratives as the policy response.
relevance_reason: High-level policy mandate for exactly what your system attempts — matching extremist narratives with persuasive non-radical dialogue; also motivates why purely ideological counter-arguments are insufficient.

title: How and Why We Should Take Deradicalization Seriously
summary: Argues that deradicalization programmes lack evaluation standards and coherent theories of change; identifies measurement of success as a critical unsolved problem and critiques both theological and psychological approaches as insufficient.
relevance_reason: High-impact citation establishing that the field lacks rigorous evaluation — directly motivates our controlled experimental design; also critiques existing intervention approaches in ways that create space for structured conversational technique recommendation.

authors: Davies, G., Neudecker, C., Ouellet, M., Bouchard, M., & Ducol, B.
title: Toward a Framework Understanding of Online Programs for Countering Violent Extremism
summary: Reviews online CVE programs finding they lack theoretical foundations and fail to address why extremist narratives resonate for particular individuals; typologizes counter-messaging approaches along a spectrum from strategic communications to counter-narratives.
relevance_reason: Motivates individualized adaptive dialogue over broadcast counter-narratives; your system addresses the gap this paper identifies — adapting to why a narrative resonates for a specific individual rather than targeting narrative content generically.

title: Countering Disinformation Effectively: An Evidence-Based Policy Guide
primary_venue: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace (policy report)
summary: Evidence-based policy review of ten disinformation counter-intervention types finding no silver bullet; counter-messaging effectiveness depends on matching receptive audiences with credible speakers and none of the approaches are simultaneously well-studied effective and scalable.
relevance_reason: Systematic evidence that broadcast and platform-level disinformation interventions have known failure modes; motivates individualized adaptive dialogue as the next step beyond what current policy tools can achieve.

title: Assessing Outcomes of Online Campaigns Countering Violent Extremism: A Case Study of the Redirect Method
summary: Reviews evaluations of online CVE campaigns finding virtually all focus on reach and engagement rather than attitude or behavior change; case study of the Redirect Method shows it successfully placed content in front of users but could not demonstrate impact on attitudes.
relevance_reason: Establishes the process-vs-impact evaluation gap your directional accuracy metric directly addresses; the Redirect Method's evaluation failure is precisely what your controlled experimental design overcomes.
